title: TIAA’s AI flags a suspected scam involving a 76-year-old’s retirement savings, and staff stop the money from moving
summary: TIAA’s CEO said that an unnamed AI tool flagged a 76-year-old’s unusual withdrawal and that staff then kept his retirement savings of more than $3 million from moving.
account: In a Forbes piece of 8 March 2026, Sastry Durvasula, TIAA's chief operating, information and digital officer, describes AI alerts that send suspected scams to customer care staff and the fraud department. The piece does not mention the 76-year-old's case. On 17 June 2026, in an episode of the Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry podcast, TIAA CEO Thasunda Brown Duckett told Fortune that an AI alert helped staff stop a scam involving a 76-year-old participant’s retirement savings. Fortune's first article on the podcast, published the same day, reports that the participant was trying to withdraw his entire $3 million portfolio. It quotes Duckett as saying that AI by itself would not necessarily have protected him. Fortune published a lightly edited transcript of the interview on 22 June 2026. In the interview, Duckett says that a portfolio manager referred the concern to the fraud team, which spent hours with the participant and contacted his daughter. She says that the money did not move. The transcript describes retirement holdings above $3 million and does not itemize an attempted transfer. No participant statement, transaction record, or separate investigation is supplied.
purpose: TIAA uses an unnamed AI tool to flag suspected scams and send alerts to customer care staff, who connect the case to the fraud department.
system: Unnamed TIAA AI tool used to flag suspected fraud for human review

ai_role.statement: According to TIAA's CEO, an AI tool raised the first flag on an out-of-pattern withdrawal. A portfolio manager escalated it, the fraud team spent hours with the participant, and a fraud specialist reached his daughter before the money was stopped. The CEO says that AI by itself would not necessarily have protected him. The account comes from the deployer, and no source shows what would have happened without the flag.

fields.summary: TIAA’s CEO said that an unnamed AI tool flagged a 76-year-old’s unusual withdrawal and that staff then kept his retirement savings of more than $3 million from moving.
fields.account: In a Forbes piece of 8 March 2026, Sastry Durvasula, TIAA's chief operating, information and digital officer, describes AI alerts that send suspected scams to customer care staff and the fraud department. The piece does not mention the 76-year-old's case. On 17 June 2026, in an episode of the Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry podcast, TIAA CEO Thasunda Brown Duckett told Fortune that an AI alert helped staff stop a scam involving a 76-year-old participant’s retirement savings. Fortune's first article on the podcast, published the same day, reports that the participant was trying to withdraw his entire $3 million portfolio. It quotes Duckett as saying that AI by itself would not necessarily have protected him. Fortune published a lightly edited transcript of the interview on 22 June 2026. In the interview, Duckett says that a portfolio manager referred the concern to the fraud team, which spent hours with the participant and contacted his daughter. She says that the money did not move. The transcript describes retirement holdings above $3 million and does not itemize an attempted transfer. No participant statement, transaction record, or separate investigation is supplied.

value.text: The AI raised the concern, but employees investigated and persuaded the participant with help from his daughter before money moved.
